trickyParts: The version columns are int4; a 14-digit timestamp needs bigint. The daemon's schema_version is created by migration 0001, so the runner widens it inside the first timestamped migration's transaction; Dispatch's schema_migrations is created by the runner, so createVersionTable creates bigint and widens an existing integer under its lock.
pgx encodes a parameter for the column type it finds, so the exists check and the insert cast $1::bigint, or a 14-digit version is refused client-side before the widening runs.

A connection that prepared max(version) while the column was integer fails once after the widening (cached plan must not change result type): the daemon's SchemaVersion and Dispatch's Healthy cast the result to bigint. The live upgrade proof found the Dispatch case (140 -> 0); TestHealthyAnswersAcrossTheWideningOfTheVersionColumn reproduces it.
The secrets broker also uses pgmigrate; it stays numbered (CheckNumberedOneToN, integer column), and its tests pass.
deviations: Duplicate-identifier refusals already existed in both loaders; this round adds a timestamped-pair case to each, and a CheckIdentifiers rule (numbered 1..last each once, every later version a real 14-digit UTC instant) that replaces Dispatch's TestMigrationSetIsNumberedOneToN.
Two docs/solutions learnings about renumbering are marked superseded in their front matter.
discoveredComplexity: The pod's test Postgres is a rootless PostgreSQL 18.6 (zonky binaries, as scripts/dispatch/README.md stands one up) with pgvector 0.8.7 from the PGDG package, on 127.0.0.1:55432; the census tests that append &search_path need a DSN with a query string (?sslmode=disable).
